summary: A short note from Postel and Kline pointing out that TENEX systems use link numbers outside the allowed range, which violates the official Host-Host protocol. This causes problems for some sites trying to connect, and the authors urge bringing TENEX into conformance.

eli5.summary: A group is using road lanes that are not allowed, which confuses other drivers. The note asks them to follow the rules.

subtitle: Warning about TENEX link number violations of the Host-Host protocol

tldr.problem: TENEX systems are using link numbers that fall outside the range allowed by the official Host-Host protocol, causing connection failures with other sites.
tldr.mechanism: The Host-Host protocol defines valid link number ranges that TENEX is violating.
tldr.outcome: The authors urge TENEX system maintainers to correct their implementations to follow the established protocol standard.

today: RFC 417 was a protocol compliance notice from November 1972. It was not updated or superseded, though it addressed a specific implementation issue.

sections.title: Link Number Violations
sections.content: TENEX systems on ARPANET are using link numbers outside the allowed range defined by the official Host-Host protocol. This violates the established protocol specification and causes problems when other sites attempt to establish connections with TENEX systems.
sections.eli5: TENEX computers are not following the network rules about which connection numbers they can use.

sections.title: Protocol Requirement and Consequences
sections.content: The Host-Host protocol specifies which link numbers are valid for inter-host communication. When TENEX systems use numbers outside this range, other sites' connection attempts fail because their software expects standard link numbers. This incompatibility prevents successful communication between TENEX and other hosts.
sections.eli5: When computers talk to each other, they use numbered connections. TENEX is using wrong numbers, so other computers cannot understand it.

sections.title: Call for Correction
sections.content: The authors, Postel and Kline, urge that all TENEX systems be brought into conformance with the official Host-Host protocol. This requires correcting the link number assignments in TENEX implementations.
sections.eli5: The authors ask TENEX maintainers to fix their systems to follow the rules.
